findings.asked: Use bounds of a distance and a time (in hours and minutes) to find a maximum average speed.
findings.wentWrong: A minority finished. The time bound was the obstacle: candidates bounded 70.5 minutes, or wrote 1 h 10.5 min as 1.105 h.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Converted the time to decimal hours, bounded it, then divided the upper distance by the lower time keeping the full display.
findings.rule: Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60 before finding bounds; max speed = max distance / min time.

findings.asked: Substitute bounds into a formula of the form v squared = u squared + 2as.
findings.wentWrong: Bounds were mostly identified. Errors were in the formula itself (u not squared, a not doubled); the weakest just substituted the given values.
findings.rule: Write the four bounds, then substitute the combination that maximises the target, using the formula exactly.

findings.asked: Bounds in a formula to find a maximum value.
findings.wentWrong: Improving year on year; the same formula slips (V not squared, g not doubled) and rounding errors at the end.
findings.rule: Read the formula symbol by symbol; keep the full display.

findings.asked: Maximum number of items given a total mass to the nearest 100 kg and an item mass to the nearest 5 kg.
findings.wentWrong: The nearest-5 bound was the problem: 45 was used instead of 47.5. Many did get the upper bound 1550. Some did not give a whole number, or rounded up when a maximum count must round down.
findings.rule: Half of 5 is 2.5; a maximum number of whole items is rounded down.

findings.wentWrong: About 30% got full marks. Many calculated with the given values and then bounded the answer; some used both upper bounds where the subtraction needed one upper and one lower; most rounded the result (3.86) instead of leaving the whole display.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Listed all four bounds, chose upper hypotenuse with lower leg for the maximum, and left the full display as the bound.
findings.rule: Bound the inputs, not the output; in a subtraction pair the biggest with the smallest.

ruleToRemember: Write all four bounds first; subtraction and division mix an upper with a lower; convert units (minutes to decimal hours) before bounding; keep the full calculator display for a bound and round a maximum count down.
aStarSignal: Bounds threaded through a two-stage calculation (a formula or Pythagoras, or a speed with a time in hours and minutes) with the right max/min pairing at each stage.
